ledger.note: 1101: Vitebsk becomes a principality under Sviatoslav Vseslavich when Polotsk is divided. 'Following the death of Vseslav of Polotsk in 1101, Polotsk was divided into six smaller principalities'; 'Sviatoslav Vseslavich inherited the lands surrounding Vitebsk and started the Vitebsk branch'. Repair pass: the region is the Vitebsk fief (60 km round Vitsyebsk inside the core), not Cliopatria's whole row, which is the Polotsk-Vitebsk core; it is the part of the Polotsk dossier's 1101 split disc inside that core.

region.text: Vitebsk, annexed with Polotsk by Mstislav of Kiev

ledger.note: 1129: Mstislav of Kiev annexes Polotsk and its vassals, Vitebsk among them. 'In 1127, the prince of Kyiv, Mstislav Vladimirovich, began a war with the princes of Polotsk over trade routes'; in 1129 he 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk'. The princes' list keeps a Vitebsk prince (Vasilko Sviatoslavich 1129-1132), so the hold may have been an overlordship.

region.text: Vitebsk, back under its own line

ledger.note: 1132: Vitebsk's prince is invited to claim Polotsk and the Kievan hold lapses. 'In 1132, the residents of Polotsk ... invited Vasilko to claim the Principality of Polotsk' (Vasilko Sviatoslavich of Vitebsk in the list); 'the other exiled Polotsk princes were allowed to return in 1139'. The page does not say in words that Vitebsk left Kiev's hand in 1132.

region.text: Vitebsk, 'shortly acquired by the princes of Smolensk'

ledger.note: 1165: the princes of Smolensk acquire Vitebsk. 'In 1165-1167 due to the feudal strife, the principality of Vitebsk was shortly acquired by the princes of Smolensk'; the list shows Davyd Rostislavich 1165-1167.

region.text: Vitebsk, independent again under Briachislav Vasilkovich

1195: the princes march on Smolensk and Vitebsk returns to Polotsk. 'who in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk'; as a result 'Vitebsk again fell under the rule of Polotsk'.

notes: Pages opened: 2 of up to 2. Infobox area: none ('No area value is given'). END: Cliopatria's last Vitebsk shape is 1177-1187 and the Polotsk dossier records the absorption in 1195 ('Vitebsk again fell under the rule of Polotsk'); this dossier ends there. The Vitebsk page keeps princes of the Vseslavich line in Vitebsk after 1195 (Vasilko Briachislavich to 1221, Briachislav to 1232, a gap 1232-1262, Constantine Bezrukiy 1262, Vasilko Briachislavich to 1320) under Polotsk and then Mindaugas's nephew Tautvilas (1254) and Lithuania, and incorporates Vitebsk into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1320 (Algirdas by marriage; infobox disestablished 1508). A gap-filler may prefer a vassal tint for Vitebsk inside Polotsk 1195-1320; the Lithuanian dossier has the 1318 gain. CLIOPATRIA: its Minsk row 1260-1313 and its Polotsk row 1202-1249 both contain the whole Vitebsk shape; the Minsk dossier removes it from Minsk. Cliopatria's Smolensk row draws the Vitebsk land as Smolensk's from 1188 to 1201; the pages give 1186-1195 as influence ending with Polotsk's march. The 1129 and 1165 changes of hand are on the page but Cliopatria draws Vitebsk continuously. The Kievan Rus' dossier should carry the matching 1129 gain, the Smolensk dossier the 1165-1168 hold. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-31: (1) REGION. Cliopatria's Principality of Vitebsk row (34,385 km2, 164 grid cells, bbox 27.29-30.97E 54.95-57.08N) is the Polotsk-Vitebsk core, identical to Cliopatria's Polotsk shape of 1202 and to the Minsk dossier's measurement; the page says only that Sviatoslav 'inherited the lands surrounding Vitebsk' and gives no extent or area. Every keyframe, ledger region, war zone and predecessor/successor land now draws the Vitebsk fief only: the 60 km disc round Vitsyebsk intersected with the core (31 cells, about 6,500 km2), the exact complement of the Polotsk dossier's 1101-1194 keyframe (the core minus the same disc, 133 cells), so the town of Polotsk and its land are no longer drawn twice. The 60 km radius is the Polotsk dossier's convention, not a page's figure. K1 and K2 (the two Cliopatria shapes) are verdict wrong; K0 and K3 are new keyframes. (2) RULERS. The page prints overlapping terms (Vseslav 1132-1164 with Roman 1162-1165; Briachislav 1178-1181 with Vseslav 1180-1186; its own remark: the list has overlapping dates). Spans are cut to be contiguous (Vseslav to 1162, Briachislav to 1180); the printed years are in each ruler's note. (3) 1195-1320, NOT ADDED (disagreement with the reviewer's thin item). The page: 'Vitebsk again fell under the rule of Polotsk' (1195); 'in 1254, the nephew of Mindaugas, Tautvilas was given Polotsk'; Tautvilas 'placed his son Constantine as ruler of Vitebsk in 1262'; princes' list Vasilko Briachislavich 1297-1320; 'Jaroslav died in 1320 without heirs and Vitebsk was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' (intro: 'nominally inherited into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1320'); 1508 voivodeship. A Vitebsk dependency span for 1195-1306 would draw land the Polotsk dossier already holds as Polotsk's own (its keyframes 1195-1306 are the whole core, 'includes both Polotsk and Vitebsk') and the Lithuanian dossier already draws as vassal land from 1240 (vassal_start region 'Polotsk and the Vitebsk land'), so it would be drawn a third time; the page itself says 'under the rule of Polotsk'. The only stretch nobody draws is 1307-1317 (Lithuania gains a Polotsk disc in 1307 and Vitebsk only in 1318): that needs the Polotsk dossier to subtract the Vitebsk disc from its 1195-1306 keyframes and a second Vitebsk span, which belongs to the orchestrator or a gap-filler. The page gives no 1318 (the Lithuanian dossier's date comes from the Algirdas page; the Vitebsk list has Algirdas from 1320). (4) COUNTERPARTS unchanged: 1129/1132 name kievan-rus where the Polotsk dossier names principality-of-kiev; Smolensk records its 1165-1168 and 1186-1195 events against principality-of-polotsky, not principality-of-vitebsk.
